description: Answer key for the synthetic sample-c-doublefree target (CHT stream reader). Kept under output/samples/sample-c-doublefree/ — NOT inside targets/samples/sample-c-doublefree/ — so the audited agents are not handed the answer while being measured. The deterministic scorer reads it after the run. This target isolates a double-free reached from attacker bytes alone, so double-free recall can be measured directly. Its configured AddressSanitizer build reproduces that bug; the release-only overflow behind the assert trap is scored through source findings. The two false-positive traps measure precision.

planted_bugs.modeled_on: classic error-path double free (CWE-415) — a failure path releases an owner the caller's cleanup releases again
planted_bugs.summary: PUSH's over-long-payload failure path frees ctx->chunk and returns -1 without clearing the owner; cht_read breaks out of the pass and frees ctx.chunk again in its exit cleanup. A stream of OPEN(cap) followed by a PUSH larger than cap is the whole reproducer. The buffer is never dereferenced after the first free, so the defect surfaces only as a double-free (the freeing frame is handle_push; the faulting frame ASan reports is cht_read).

planted_bugs.modeled_on: a debug-only invariant guarding a fixed copy — assert() compiled out by -DNDEBUG leaves an unchecked memcpy
planted_bugs.summary: The TRAIL handler checks its field against the 32-byte buffer retained in the stack-resident decoder context with assert() alone, then memcpy()s it. A supported release build (-DNDEBUG) compiles the check out, so an over-long TRAIL field overflows that buffer and the stack frame around it. The configured sanitizer build keeps asserts on, so this source-proven release bug is scored as a finding; the ABRT the assert raises in the configured build is the debug-only-assert trap.

false_positive_traps.refute_reason: The NOTE value pointer is dereferenced only inside the branch guarded by memcmp(val, "on", 2) == 0, so a non-"on" value returns before any dereference. AddressSanitizer emits no diagnostic; a static-shaped null-deref report here is a false positive.

A TRAIL field longer than its 32-byte retained buffer trips assert() and aborts before the copy. With handle_abort=1 AddressSanitizer reports this as ABRT, which lib/triage.py autodiscards: an assertion failure is a debug invariant check, not a memory-safety fault. Only an ABRT in this frame counts as the trap firing; a real overflow here (a release build with -DNDEBUG) is the planted release-build-trail-overflow bug.
